method: source-to-sink review of every ITEM; no requests were sent and no container was started
environment_notes: No PHP binary is available in this audit environment (which php -> exit 1), so PHP runtime semantics that could not be proven from source were marked [Needs Verification] instead of being asserted.
Real .env values were never read or printed; only .env.example placeholders were inspected.

Global install-state gate: app/Http/Middleware/DujiaoBoot.php:19-23 redirects all dujiaoka.boot routes to /install while install.lock is missing, and app/Http/Middleware/InstallCheck.php:19-23 blocks /install once it exists. PQ-01/PQ-02/PQ-04/PQ-05/PQ-12 require install.lock present; PQ-03 requires it absent.

findings.title: Yipay (epay) notify signature is verified with the public placeholder secret stored by install.sql ('密钥'), so an anonymous attacker can forge a notification and complete its own order to take the cards
findings.source: GET /pay/yipay/notify_url query parameters -> $request->all() (app/Http/Controllers/Pay/YipayController.php:61); the attacker also picks the order's pay_id via the order-creation field payway (app/Http/Controllers/Home/OrderController.php:75 -> app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:135-138)
findings.sink: md5(sign . $payGateway->merchant_pem) plus hash_equals (app/Http/Controllers/Pay/YipayController.php:94-95) -> OrderProcessService::completedOrder() at :101 -> processAuto() card delivery
findings.reachability: Anonymous. routes/common/pay.php:28 registers GET pay/yipay/notify_url inside the web group (app/Providers/RouteServiceProvider.php:61); the only route middleware is dujiaoka.pay_gate_way whose handler is a pass-through (app/Http/Middleware/PayGateWay.php:17-20). GET is not CSRF-checked and pay/*/notify_url is additionally listed in the CSRF except array (app/Http/Middleware/VerifyCsrfToken.php:21-26).
findings.preconditions: 1) install.lock present (installed instance). 2) The pays row bound to the attacker's order still carries the shipped placeholder merchant_pem '密钥' (database/sql/install.sql:515-517) - which is exactly the post-install default, because install.sql:539-540 disables every channel and enables only /pay/yipay. 3) A stocked automatic-delivery goods item exists. If the operator replaced merchant_pem with the real epay secret, the forgery fails.
findings.impact: Anonymous order completion without any payment: the attacker can drain stocked card secrets order by order (financial loss equal to the goods value).
findings.evidence: EVID_AUTH_PATH_MATCH: routes/common/pay.php:28 - Route::get('yipay/notify_url', 'YipayController@notifyUrl'); no auth middleware; app/Http/Middleware/PayGateWay.php:17-20 returns $next($request). EVID_AUTH_PERMISSION_CHECK: app/Http/Controllers/Pay/YipayController.php:62-95 - only structural checks (hasRequiredFields, order exists, gateway exists, isExpectedGatewayRoute('/pay/yipay'), optional trade_status/status) then md5($sign . $payGateway->merchant_pem) compared with hash_equals. EVID_CRYPTO_KEY_MANAGEMENT: database/sql/install.sql:484-500 defines the pays columns (position 8 = merchant_pem) and database/sql/install.sql:515 inserts (14,'易支付-支付宝','alipay',1,1,'商户号','','密钥','/pay/yipay',2,...) so merchant_pem = '密钥' (a public literal, not a secret). database/sql/install.sql:538-540 - 'Only enable epay (yipay) by default': UPDATE pays SET is_open=0; UPDATE pays SET is_open=1 WHERE pay_handleroute='/pay/yipay'. EVID_BIZ_STATE_PERSISTENCE: app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:423-434 (actual_price/trade_no persisted, processAuto at :428) and :509-527 (cards selected, order->info filled with card secrets, status=STATUS_COMPLETED, cards marked sold). EVID_LEAK_ACCESS_PATH: the secrets are rendered back to the buyer at app/Http/Controllers/Home/OrderController.php:171-179 -> resources/views/unicorn/static_pages/orderinfo.blade.php:83-85 (also hyper:97-98, luna:112-114). Attack arithmetic: sign = md5(ksort-ed non-empty k=v pairs joined by '&' . '密钥') is computable offline; the amount check app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:418-422 compares the order price with the attacker-supplied money value the attacker already knows. [Not obtained: no dynamic request was sent, MODE=static]
findings.non_vuln_analysis: hash_equals is used (timing-safe), amounts are bccomp-checked, the gateway route is pinned with isExpectedGatewayRoute, and the signature covers all request parameters - so the scheme is sound and the defect is purely the key source. A properly configured store (real epay secret in merchant_pem) cannot be forged this way, which is why impact is 3 but complexity is scored 1 (operator-side precondition).
findings.remediation: Before computing the signature, reject callbacks whose channel secret is empty, shorter than a sane minimum, or equal to a known installer placeholder ('密钥', '商户私钥', 'V 免签通讯密钥'); additionally confirm the payment through the epay server-side query API and bind the callback to the order with a server-side nonce. Ship install.sql with every channel is_open=0 and force real credentials before enabling a channel.

cvss_like.reason: Anonymous single GET; impact is free goods; complexity reduced by the operator-side precondition (placeholder key).

findings.title: completedOrder() has no row lock or unique constraint, and OrderExpired updates unconditionally: concurrent callbacks repeat side effects and the expiry job can overwrite a just-paid order with STATUS_EXPIRED
findings.source: Six gateway notify endpoints (routes/common/pay.php:18,21,25,28,32,41,44,48) and the zero-price path app/Http/Controllers/PayController.php:190-196 (completedOrder with trade_no 'FREE-' . order_sn); delayed job app/Jobs/OrderExpired.php:53-61 dispatched at app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:364
findings.sink: app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:392-434 - DB::beginTransaction(); order loaded by a plain first() (app/Service/OrderService.php:212-216); status branch at :399; trade_no duplicate query at :411-417; processAuto/processManual at :427-431; commit at :434. No lockForUpdate/sharedLock anywhere and no unique index on orders.trade_no (database/sql/install.sql:444-472). Second sink: app/Service/OrderService.php:228-231 expiredOrderSN() -> UPDATE by order_sn only.
findings.reachability: Anonymous for the notify paths (see PQ-01 reachability). The expiry race is triggered only by a legitimate payment landing in the same window as the queued expiry job.
findings.preconditions: install.lock present. Duplicate-notify variant: gateway retries or two simultaneous notifications for one order (the handler returns 'fail' on every exception, app/Http/Controllers/Pay/YipayController.php:100-108, which invites retries). Expiry variant: payment notify arriving inside the sub-second window between app/Jobs/OrderExpired.php:56 (read) and :58 (unconditional update).
findings.impact: Data integrity / financial correctness: (a) a paid and already-delivered order can be flipped to STATUS_EXPIRED (-1) and its coupon returned, so the order page and any operator workflow treat it as unpaid; (b) duplicated side effects when a notification is processed twice: salesVolumeIncr (app/Service/GoodsService.php:147-150), duplicate card_send_user_email / manual_send_manage_mail dispatch (app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:539-542, 491-495) and duplicate push/webhook dispatch (:436-452). Distinct-card double issuing was NOT proven (see rejected PQ-02a).
findings.evidence: EVID_RACE_CRITICAL_SECTION: app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:392-434 - read (395) -> check (399) -> write (423-431) with no SELECT ... FOR UPDATE; the transaction gives atomicity but not mutual exclusion for the status transition. EVID_RACE_SHARED_RESOURCE: the orders row keyed by order_sn (UNIQUE idx_order_sn, database/sql/install.sql:469) plus carmis rows (app/Service/CarmisService.php:29-37 select-then-update, :49-52). EVID_RACE_WINDOW_ANALYSIS: database/sql/install.sql:444-472 declares only PRIMARY KEY(id), UNIQUE(order_sn), idx_goods_id and idex_email - no unique key on trade_no, so the :411-417 pre-check is advisory; app/Service/OrderService.php:228-231 issues Order::query()->where('order_sn',$orderSN)->update(['status'=>STATUS_EXPIRED]) with no status guard, so it overwrites a concurrently completed order; app/Jobs/OrderExpired.php:56-58 separates the status check from the write. EVID_RACE_STATISTICAL_RESULT: [Not obtained - MODE=static, no container, the >=20 concurrency runs demanded by anti_hallucination Rule 11 could not be executed]. Consequence: verdict kept at suspected and severity capped at medium.
findings.non_vuln_analysis: InnoDB row locks serialise the later UPDATE, so the second writer normally observes the same card rows and rewrites the same values (idempotent info/status/trade_no); epay retries with the same trade_no, and the definite-duplicate branch at :399-410 acknowledges repeats once the first transaction has committed. No dynamic evidence was collected, so this is an integrity/hardening issue rather than a demonstrated exploit.
findings.remediation: Load the order with ->lockForUpdate() inside the transaction (or use where('status', STATUS_WAIT_PAY)->update([...]) and abort when 0 rows change); add a UNIQUE index on orders.trade_no; make expiredOrderSN() conditional (`->where('order_sn',$sn)->where('status',Order::STATUS_WAIT_PAY)->update([...])`) and re-read the status in the job immediately before the update.

cvss_like.reason: Reachable anonymously but exploitation needs a race window; impact is state corruption rather than disclosure; capped because Rule 11 statistical evidence is unavailable in static mode.

findings.title: With install.lock absent, the unauthenticated installer imports install.sql (mass DROP TABLE) and rewrites admin_users id=1 to attacker credentials; the .env overwrite is partially hardened
findings.source: GET /install and POST /do-install, anonymous, gated only by the install.check middleware (routes/common/web.php:37-42)
findings.sink: app/Http/Controllers/Home/HomeController.php:202 file_put_contents(.env) -> :204 DB::unprepared(file_get_contents(database/sql/install.sql)) -> :206-214 DB::table('admin_users')->where('id',1)->update(username, bcrypt(password)) -> :216 install.lock write; secondary sinks :179 MySQL connect and :181-182 Redis set/get against attacker-supplied hosts
findings.reachability: Anonymous. app/Http/Middleware/InstallCheck.php:19-23 blocks only when base_path()/install.lock exists; install.lock is absent from the repository tree (git-ignored via .gitignore:15 and .dockerignore:13) and is created only by container start-up logic (Dockerfile:11-17, conf/start.sh:28-30).
findings.preconditions: install.lock absent at request time: (a) any non-container deployment (nginx+php-fpm, shared hosting, artisan serve); (b) the Docker image while started with INSTALL=true (Dockerfile:14 and conf/start.sh:28 skip lock creation when INSTALL=true; docker-compose.yml:17-18 defaults it to false). The compose bind-mount at docker-compose.yml:13 also leaves the lock path as a directory when the host file does not exist, which blocks the installer in that specific setup.
findings.impact: Mass data destruction (install.sql drops every table, e.g. database/sql/install.sql:484 DROP TABLE IF EXISTS `pays`) plus full admin takeover: :206-214 sets admin_users.id=1 username/password to attacker values, so the attacker reaches the admin panel even when the .env write fails. It also re-seeds every gateway row with the public placeholder secret (amplifier for PQ-01).
findings.evidence: EVID_AUTH_PATH_MATCH: routes/common/web.php:37-42 - Route::group(['middleware'=>['install.check'],'namespace'=>'Home'], ... Route::get('install',...) and Route::post('do-install',...)); app/Http/Kernel.php:71 maps install.check. EVID_AUTH_PERMISSION_CHECK: app/Http/Middleware/InstallCheck.php:19-23 - if (file_exists($installLock)) { return redirect(url('/')); } return $next($request); - the sole gate. EVID_WRITE_CALLSITE: app/Http/Controllers/Home/HomeController.php:202 file_put_contents($envPath, $envTemp, LOCK_EX). EVID_WRITE_CONTENT_SOURCE: :188-200 substitutes every {placeholder} in .env.example with $request->all() values; the hardened code escapes backslash, double quote and dollar (:196-198) and rejects CRLF in the 11 placeholder fields (:138-145), so plain CRLF env injection is fixed. EVID_BIZ_STATE_PERSISTENCE: :204 DB::unprepared(install.sql) runs unconditionally (its return value is ignored) and :206-214 rewrites the admin row, treating a non-1 affected-row count as failure (:212-214). EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: .env.example:1-21,45 - the only placeholders are APP_NAME, APP_KEY, DB_*, REDIS_* and ADMIN_ROUTE_PREFIX, all inside the CRLF-filtered list. [Not obtained: no live instance in MODE=static]
findings.non_vuln_analysis: Three genuine mitigations exist and are why this is not critical: (1) Docker start-up writes install.lock automatically unless INSTALL=true (Dockerfile:14, conf/start.sh:28-30); (2) .env values are escaped and CRLF-filtered now; (3) in the official image /app is root-owned with 0644 files (Dockerfile:22-28) while PHP runs as 'application', so the .env and lock writes fail with a warning - but the destructive SQL import and the admin_users reset at :204-214 do not depend on that write and still execute. Residual hardening gap [Needs Verification]: the CRLF guard casts with (string) $request->input($field) at :142, so an array-typed parameter (db_host[]=... / title[]=...) evaluates to the literal 'Array' and passes the guard, after which str_replace at :199 substitutes the array element verbatim into .env; the array-to-string behaviour could not be executed (no PHP binary available) and reaching :199 additionally requires successful MySQL and Redis connections at :179-182, so it is recorded as defence-in-depth, not as a confirmed bypass.
findings.remediation: Serve the installer only behind an explicit operator switch (INSTALL=true env or a CLI-only artisan command); create the lock atomically with fopen('x') as the first action so the installer can run at most once; abort when file_put_contents fails instead of continuing to DB::unprepared; validate db_host/redis_host with filter_var (IP/domain) and reject private, loopback and link-local ranges; substitute only strings (is_string($item) ? $item : '').

cvss_like.reason: Anonymous single POST; impact is full takeover plus mass table drop; complexity reduced by the deployment-specific install.lock precondition.

findings.title: Installer connects to attacker-supplied db_host/redis_host without target validation (anonymous internal probe plus blind Redis write)
findings.source: POST /do-install body fields db_host, db_port, redis_host, redis_port, redis_password (app/Http/Controllers/Home/HomeController.php:161-176)
findings.sink: app/Http/Controllers/Home/HomeController.php:179 DB::connection()->select('select 1 limit 1') and :181-182 Redis::set('dujiaoka_com','ok') / Redis::get(...) against the attacker-supplied host:port
findings.reachability: Anonymous, same install.check gate as PQ-03 (install.lock absent).
findings.preconditions: install.lock absent. The error handling forms a three-way oracle: :218 RedisException -> 'Redis 配置错误', :221 QueryException -> '数据库配置错误', :224 other -> '安装失败'.
findings.impact: Internal service enumeration (MySQL/Redis handshake success distinguishes open ports and protocol type) and, where an unauthenticated Redis is reachable, a blind write of key dujiaoka_com=ok into it (Redis::set at :181) with an attacker-chosen redis_password. No internal response body is returned, so the primitive is limited.
findings.evidence: EVID_SSRF_FINAL_URL: app/Http/Controllers/Home/HomeController.php:161-176 - host/port/password taken verbatim from the request and merged into config('database.connections.mysql') and config('database.redis.default'); prior validation is only the CRLF regex at :138-145, with no IP/domain allow-list and no private-range block. EVID_SSRF_URL_NORMALIZATION: none - DB::purge() at :177 then DB::connection() at :179. EVID_SSRF_DNS_INNER_BLOCK: absent (no filter_var/gethostbyname anywhere in the file). EVID_SSRF_EXECUTION_RESPONSE: [Not obtained - MODE=static, no container]. non-vuln factor: messages are generic, but :218 versus :221 still separates failure classes.
findings.remediation: Validate db_host/redis_host with filter_var (FILTER_VALIDATE_IP / FILTER_VALIDATE_DOMAIN), reject 127.0.0.0/8, 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 169.254/16 and ::1 after resolution, and require authentication for the installer.

cvss_like.reason: Anonymous but gated by install.lock absence; impact limited to internal probing and a blind Redis write.

findings.title: Anonymous e-mail order lookup returns plaintext card secrets with no ownership proof and no rate limit (is_open_search_pwd defaults to closed)
findings.sink: app/Service/OrderService.php:259-269 withEmailAndPassword() - WHERE email = ? only, no owner/session predicate - rendered with card secrets by resources/views/*/static_pages/orderinfo.blade.php
findings.reachability: Anonymous. routes/common/web.php:12,32 - inside the dujiaoka.boot group, no auth middleware; the POST needs a CSRF token that any visitor obtains from the public order-search page in its own session. No throttle middleware exists on the web group (app/Http/Kernel.php:34-43).
findings.preconditions: 1) install.lock present. 2) The attacker knows or guesses a customer e-mail address. 3) dujiaoka_config_get('is_open_search_pwd', STATUS_CLOSE) is not enabled - the default, since STATUS_CLOSE is 0 (app/Models/BaseModel.php:18) and install.sql contains no is_open_search_pwd row, so the helper default at app/Helpers/functions.php:58-62 applies. If the operator enables the search password, :211-213 requires the customer-chosen per-order search_pwd, which is compared by plain equality (app/Service/OrderService.php:263-265) and is frequently empty.
findings.impact: Disclosure of up to the 5 most recent orders of any e-mail address, including orders.info which holds the plaintext card secrets of completed orders, plus buyer IP and timestamps. Any customer's purchased cards can be stolen anonymously; the cards are already marked sold, so the victim has no recourse.
findings.evidence: EVID_AUTH_PATH_MATCH: routes/common/web.php:32 Route::post('search-order-by-email','OrderController@searchOrderByEmail'); app/Http/Kernel.php:34-43 web group has session/CSRF only. EVID_AUTH_PERMISSION_CHECK: app/Http/Controllers/Home/OrderController.php:208-216 - the only branch is (dujiaoka_config_get('is_open_search_pwd', STATUS_CLOSE) == STATUS_OPEN && !$request->has('search_pwd')); an e-mail-only search is allowed in the default state. EVID_AUTH_IDOR_OWNERSHIP: app/Service/OrderService.php:261-268 - Order::query()->where('email',$email)->when(!empty($searchPwd), ...)->orderBy('created_at','DESC')->take(5)->get(); there is no session, cookie, IP or ownership predicate and the caller's dujiaoka_orders cookie (set at app/Http/Controllers/Home/OrderController.php:98-109) is never consulted. EVID_LEAK_SOURCE_POINT + EVID_LEAK_DATA_TYPE: card secrets are stored into orders.info by app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:520-524 ($order->info = implode(PHP_EOL, $carmisInfo)) and printed raw at resources/views/unicorn/static_pages/orderinfo.blade.php:83-85 (hyper:97-98, luna:112-114). EVID_LEAK_ACCESS_PATH: rendered by app/Http/Controllers/Home/OrderController.php:221. EVID_LEAK_RESPONSE_CONTENT: [Not obtained - MODE=static, no instance was queried]. No throttle anywhere in routes/common/web.php or app/Http/Kernel.php:34-43, so the customer base can be swept by e-mail.
findings.non_vuln_analysis: CSRF is enforced on the POST and the SQL is parameterised, but neither blocks the disclosure; the auth check is conditional on a config flag that is off by default. The alternative vector /detail-order-sn/{orderSN} is not practically enumerable (rejected PQ-04a), so the e-mail lookup is the real path.
findings.remediation: Require proof of ownership before returning info: mail a one-time link/token to the address, or require the order number together with a non-empty search_pwd, and mask secrets (last 4 characters) in list views. Default is_open_search_pwd to ON, force a non-empty search_pwd at order creation, and add throttle:10,1 to the order-search routes.

cvss_like.reason: Anonymous single POST needing only a known e-mail; leaks paid secrets (data breach) but not full system compromise.

findings.title: Stripe /pay/stripe/check treats the order-context token as optional and completes the order with the order price instead of the charged amount, so a cheap Source can complete an expensive order
findings.source: GET /pay/stripe/check with orderid, source and stripe_usd_amount (routes/common/pay.php:37) -> $request->all() (app/Http/Controllers/Pay/StripeController.php:476)
findings.sink: app/Http/Controllers/Pay/StripeController.php:501-513 amount validated against the attacker-supplied stripe_usd_amount, then Charge::create(); completion at :515 completedOrder($orderid, $cacheord->actual_price, $charge->id)
findings.reachability: Anonymous. routes/common/pay.php:37 - GET stripe/check in the web group, PayGateWay is a pass-through (app/Http/Middleware/PayGateWay.php:17-20), GET is not CSRF-checked and the handler returns plain text.
findings.preconditions: 1) install.lock present. 2) The Stripe pays row (database/sql/install.sql:521, id 21, pay_handleroute 'pay/stripe') is enabled - install.sql:539-540 disables it by default, so the operator must have turned Stripe on. 3) The publishable key is rendered into the gateway HTML (app/Http/Controllers/Pay/StripeController.php:32,266), so an attacker holding any order can create a Source client-side with stripe.createSource({amount, currency:'usd', owner:{name: order_sn}}) as the page itself does at :362-381 and :398-404. 4) Stripe-side minimum charge amounts may raise the paid amount above 1 cent, but it stays far below the order price.
findings.impact: Payment bypass with real financial loss: goods worth actual_price are completed and cards delivered while only the small USD amount of the forged Source is charged. The store cannot detect it because completedOrder is called with the order price rather than the charged amount.
findings.evidence: EVID_BIZ_FLOW_DESCRIPTION: app/Http/Controllers/Pay/StripeController.php:28-34 - the gateway computes $usd = bcmul(getUsdCurrency(actual_price),100,0), mints the HMAC order-context token (buildOrderContextToken, app/Http/Controllers/PayController.php:132-146) and embeds it in the JS at :380 (url: '/pay/stripe/check/?orderid=$orderid&context=$context&stripe_usd_amount=$usd&source=' + source). EVID_BIZ_BYPASS_POINT: :489-494 - if ($request->filled('context') && !$this->validateOrderContextToken(...)) - omitting context skips the HMAC binding entirely (order_sn|pay_id|price|stripe_usd_amount), and :485-488 then takes stripe_usd_amount from the request, using the server value only when absent; the Source check at :501-508 (status, currency === 'usd', amount === $stripeUsdAmount, owner->name == orderid) is therefore self-consistent with attacker-chosen values. EVID_BIZ_STATE_PERSISTENCE: :509-516 Charge::create with amount = $source_object->amount, then completedOrder($data['orderid'], $cacheord->actual_price, $charge->id); app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:418-422 compares $order->actual_price with $actualPrice, which is the same order price, so the underpayment is invisible; :423-434 persists trade_no/actual_price and runs processAuto (card delivery). Contrast the sibling endpoints: /charge at :544-548 charges the server-computed amount and /return_url at :454-459 requires amount === bcmul(actual_price,100,0) with currency 'cny'. EVID_BIZ_EXPLOIT_RESPONSE: [Not obtained - MODE=static; no Stripe account was contacted and no charge was created]
findings.non_vuln_analysis: The secret key is needed to retrieve the Source (:499) and to create the Charge (:509), so the attacker cannot fabricate a Source object; they can only create one client-side with the publishable key and must match owner name, currency and amount - all attacker-chosen once context is omitted. Two factors reduce impact without removing it: the charge is real money and Stripe enforces per-currency minimums, and the goods price is bounded by stock. If Stripe is never enabled the route is unreachable, because :495-498 requires an open pay/stripe gateway.
findings.remediation: Make the order-context token mandatory (reject when context is missing) in check(), returnUrl() and charge(); derive the expected amount only from the server-side order (bcmul(getUsdCurrency($cacheord->actual_price),100,0)) and ignore any client-supplied stripe_usd_amount; pass the converted charged amount to completedOrder, or assert it equals the order price before completing; bind the Source to the order via server-side state or metadata instead of the client-controlled owner.name.

cvss_like.reason: Anonymous GET with a few attacker-side steps (order plus Source creation); direct financial loss; complexity reduced because the Stripe channel must be configured.

findings.title: Payjs callback delegates signature verification entirely to the third-party SDK with no local re-check, and the key may be the install.sql placeholder '密钥' or empty
findings.sink: config(['payjs.key' => $payGateway->merchant_pem]) at app/Http/Controllers/Pay/PayjsController.php:63 -> md5(urldecode(http_build_query($data).'&key='.$this->key)) compared with loose == at vendor/xhat/payjs-laravel/src/Payjs.php:156-164 -> completedOrder() at app/Http/Controllers/Pay/PayjsController.php:73
findings.reachability: Anonymous POST (CSRF-exempt via app/Http/Middleware/VerifyCsrfToken.php:24 'pay/*/notify_url'), but only while the Payjs pays row (database/sql/install.sql:514, id 11, merchant_pem '密钥') is enabled - install.sql:539-540 disables it by default.
findings.preconditions: install.lock present; Payjs channel enabled; pays.merchant_pem equals the shipped placeholder '密钥' (database/sql/install.sql:514) or is empty. With a real Payjs key the forgery needs that secret and the finding collapses to a hardening note.
findings.impact: Same class as PQ-01: a forged notification completes the attacker's order and delivers cards without payment. Additionally the SDK returns the string '验签失败' on failure, which the controller only rejects through empty($notify_info['out_trade_no']) at app/Http/Controllers/Pay/PayjsController.php:65-71 - an illegal string-offset read whose PHP 8.3 behaviour could not be verified in this environment [Needs Verification] because no PHP binary is available.
findings.evidence: EVID_CRYPTO_KEY_MANAGEMENT: database/sql/install.sql:514 inserts (11,'Payjs 微信扫码','payjswescan',1,1,'商户号','','密钥','/pay/payjs',1,...) so merchant_pem='密钥' (public literal), and app/Http/Controllers/Pay/PayjsController.php:63 feeds exactly that value to the SDK. EVID_CRYPTO_ALGORITHM_USAGE: vendor/xhat/payjs-laravel/src/Payjs.php:156-164 - $sign = strtoupper(md5(urldecode(http_build_query($data).'&key='.$this->key))); return $in_sign == $sign; the whole verification is delegated to the vendored SDK with a loose comparison and no local re-check in app/Http/Controllers/Pay/PayjsController.php:64-73, whereas the hardened Yipay path uses hash_equals (app/Http/Controllers/Pay/YipayController.php:95 via app/Http/Controllers/PayController.php:123-130). EVID_BIZ_STATE_PERSISTENCE: app/Http/Controllers/Pay/PayjsController.php:72-73 -> app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:418-434. EVID_CRYPTO_EXPLOIT_PROOF: [Not obtained - MODE=static; no live Payjs merchant and no forgery was attempted]
findings.non_vuln_analysis: Amount and trade_no are not unverified: completedOrder enforces bccomp(actual_price, notified total_fee/100) at app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:418-422 and rejects a trade_no bound to another order at :411-417, and the gateway route is pinned by isExpectedGatewayRoute at app/Http/Controllers/Pay/PayjsController.php:60-62. The loose == between two 32-character hex md5 strings is not practically type-juggable (rejected PQ-12a). The residual defect is the secret source plus the absence of a local explicit verification step.
findings.remediation: Reject notifications when the channel secret is empty or a known placeholder; re-implement the signature check locally with hash_equals over the documented Payjs canonical string instead of trusting the vendor SDK; assert is_array($notify_info) before indexing it; verify the order server-side with the Payjs order query API (Payjs::check($payjs_order_id)) before completing.

cvss_like.reason: Anonymous POST, but both channel enablement and the placeholder-secret condition must hold; impact equals free goods.

rejected.title: Concurrent callbacks issue distinct cards twice (duplicate card consumption)
rejected.reason: Refuted as stated. processAuto selects cards with a plain read (app/Service/CarmisService.php:29-37) and marks them sold afterwards (:49-52), so two concurrent transactions observe the SAME unsold rows and the second delivery duplicates the same secret list into the same order instead of handing out a second set of cards. The demonstrable duplicate effects are side effects only (app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:433 salesVolumeIncr, :436-452 duplicate pushes/webhooks, :539-542 duplicate mail). A distinct double-issue claim needs dynamic proof (anti_hallucination Rule 11) that static mode cannot supply, so it is dropped from the finding.

rejected.title: Payjs loose == comparison is bypassable via type juggling (0e magic hash)
rejected.reason: Refuted. vendor/xhat/payjs-laravel/src/Payjs.php:163 compares two strtoupper(md5(...)) values; a loose-comparison bypass requires the server-computed digest to look like 0e[0-9]{30} (probability about 1e-47 per attempt, php_specific_patterns.md magic-hash section) and the attacker cannot submit a non-string (the value arrives as a scalar from request()->all()). No practical bypass, so the finding is kept only for the placeholder/empty key issue.

rejected.title: Payjs callback completes the order with an unverified total_fee / trade_no (no local amount or uniqueness check)
rejected.reason: Refuted. app/Http/Controllers/Pay/PayjsController.php:72-73 passes total_fee/100 and payjs_order_id into completedOrder(), which rejects on bccomp($order->actual_price, $actualPrice, 2) != 0 (app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:418-422) and rejects a trade_no already bound to another order (:411-417). Amount and trade-no integrity are enforced centrally, not missing.

rejected.title: Order secrets obtainable by enumerating /detail-order-sn/{orderSN}
rejected.reason: Refuted as an enumeration vector. routes/common/web.php:24 exposes the route without auth, but order_sn is strtoupper(Str::random(16)) (app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:317), i.e. about 62^16 values, and app/Service/OrderService.php:214 uses an exact equality lookup. The e-mail lookup (PQ-04) is the disclosure path.

rejected.title: Installer .env overwrite injectable via CRLF in the posted fields
rejected.reason: Refuted for plain string parameters: app/Http/Controllers/Home/HomeController.php:138-145 rejects CR/LF in all 11 fields that map to .env.example placeholders, and :196-198 escapes backslash, double quote and dollar. Only the array-typed-input edge case remains (the (string) cast at :142 yields 'Array'), and reaching it requires a successful MySQL and Redis connection first, so it is recorded as a defence-in-depth note inside PQ-03 rather than as a confirmed finding.

rejected.title: Stripe /return_url completes orders with the order price without checking the charged amount
rejected.reason: Refuted. app/Http/Controllers/Pay/StripeController.php:454-459 requires status 'chargeable', currency 'cny' and (int)$source_object->amount === (int)bcmul($cacheord->actual_price,100,0) before charging, so the charged amount is bound to the order price on that endpoint. Only /check (:485-515) loses that binding, which is what PQ-05 reports.
